split_rule: i % 8 == 0 => HOLDOUT (true holdout, never trained on)

A_fastgs.description: Official FastGS (train_base.sh per-scene Mip-NeRF360 settings), verbatim train.py loop, mult=0.5, optimizer_type=default.

B_vanilla.description: Faithful original INRIA 3DGS comparator on the SAME backend (same diff_gaussian_rasterization_fastgs rasterizer, same Scene/GaussianModel). Differs from FastGS only in: original mean-gradient clone/split densification; per-iteration dense Adam; mult=1.0 (full compact box); no final_prune_fastgs. Canonical 3DGS Mip-NeRF360 hyperparameters.
B_vanilla.comparator_justification: Official fastgs/FastGS exposes NO vanilla baseline in-repo (grep for vanilla render/densify_and_prune is empty; optimizer_type only selects default vs sparse_adam, both FastGS densification). Per task spec, the faithful vanilla/comparator is the original INRIA 3DGS the repo is forked from (LICENSE_ORIGINAL.md), run on the identical rasterizer backend so wall-time differences reflect the algorithm, not the backend.

measurement.training_wall_seconds: end-to-end python wall clock of the training loop (excludes ~40s camera load)
measurement.internal_training_time_seconds: sum of CUDA-event iter+optim timing (matches train.py 'Training time')
measurement.holdout_metrics: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS over true-holdout (test) cameras, rendered with each arm's own mult
